Subject: Marketplace vs vendor contract for pilot — procurement questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Nimbus is excited to move toward a short pilot for our analytics assistants. Procurement asked me to surface a few practical questions so they can decide whether to route this through AWS Marketplace (or Azure/GCP) versus signing a Redwood vendor contract directly. High level constraints:

- We must be on our approved vendor list and prefer a single consolidated invoice tied to our monthly cloud billing (PO number required).
- Procurement will need standard insurance and data processing addendum review — we can do those quickly, but prefer vendor terms we already accept where possible.
- We want the pilot to start within ~3 weeks; speed to PO is important.
- Nimbus is open to Redwood pursuing co-sell credits with our cloud partner if it materially reduces cost.

Specifics they asked:
1) If we buy on AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace, how does invoicing and PO handling work? Can we still get a single monthly invoice that maps to our PO?
2) If there is a reseller/transaction fee on marketplace, roughly how much is that and is Redwood willing to absorb/discount it for an initial pilot?
3) Are there limitations on custom terms (e.g., audit, data residency, SLAs) when using marketplace SKUs?
4) If we start on marketplace, how simple is migration to a direct vendor contract at renewal?

Appreciate a short write-up and recommended path so procurement can decide. I can loop in our finance lead if useful.

Cheers,

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (finance/ops) and Vanessa (accounts) so you get a compact answer plus an operational recommendation. Below is a concise comparison and our suggested path for a fast pilot with clean invoicing. Attaching a one-pager that summarizes the trade-offs.

Quick summary:
- Marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP): fastest procurement route in many enterprise procurement processes because it fits existing cloud spend controls and can be billed through your cloud invoice. However, marketplaces typically introduce a reseller/transaction fee and can limit some bespoke contract terms.
- Private/vendor contract: gives full contractual flexibility (SLA, custom data residency terms, audit rights) and typically yields better unit economics for committed volumes, but often requires direct procurement paperwork and takes longer.

Short answers to your numbered questions:
1) Invoicing & PO: AWS Marketplace can accept a PO and will bill via your AWS consolidated invoice. Azure & GCP have similar flows but mechanics differ — AWS typically shows a single line item per SKU on the AWS invoice; Azure may route through partner billing depending on the listing type. Expect a 30–45 day payment cycle lag from cloud provider to Redwood.
2) Reseller/transaction fee: marketplaces commonly include a fee (~7–15% depending on partner/reseller model). For an initial pilot we can offset some of that via a one-time credit or absorb a portion of fees; Rishi will suggest specifics below.
3) Contract limitations: marketplaces commonly restrict amendment of core offer terms (billing cadence, cancellation windows), and some marketplaces do not permit non-standard data residency or long-tail audit language. If you need specific residency or custom SLA commitments, a direct vendor addendum is safer.
4) Migration: we support migration from a marketplace purchase to a direct contract at renewal; we can map entitlements and provide a credit for prior marketplace spend to avoid double-billing.

Recommend: For speed-to-start, accept a private offer on the cloud marketplace (AWS Private Offer / Azure Managed Offer / GCP Private Catalog) so Nimbus gets PO-based consolidated billing while we preserve some negotiation flexibility (private offers can include negotiated pricing and short SOWs). At renewal, convert to a direct contract for committed discounts and SLA guarantees.

Next step: would you be open to a 30-minute call on Thursday to confirm procurement requirements (PO formatting, approved vendor clause, and any required DPA/insurance attachments)? If yes, we'll prepare a short SOW and a private-offer proposal you can route through your vendor onboarding team.

> Quick summary: marketplace fastest; private contract more flexible; recommend private offer for pilot and migrate at renewal.

Liam / Nimbus team — adding a few operational details from finance/ops perspective so procurement can evaluate tradeoffs:

- Invoicing timing & PO: If you buy via AWS Marketplace private offer, AWS invoices you and remits to Redwood. That means your AP team pays AWS (single invoice) and assigns the PO to that invoice. Redwood receives payment on AWS' payment schedule (typically net-30 to net-45 depending on your AWS billing cycle). For Azure, billing cadence can be different and sometimes goes through the reseller. GCP supports private offers but invoicing cadence and reseller flows are again provider-specific.
- Fees & economics: Marketplace takes a cut; typical observable ranges are 7–15% on list pricing. Example: a $10k monthly pilot could see $700–$1,500 go to marketplace fees. Redwood can provide a pilot credit to offset up to X% of that fee; for negotiation we usually propose absorbing up to 50% of estimated marketplace fees for a first-time pilot.
- SKUs & entitlements: Marketplaces require SKUs/offer IDs which makes per-seat or per-unit billing straightforward, but limits ability to apply line-item credits or complex crediting without a private-offer arranged.
- Compliance & terms: Marketplaces are fine for standard DPAs and SOC 2 references, but if you need bespoke residency obligations or strict SLA financial credits tied to latency percentiles for Dedicated pools, a direct contract is preferable.
- Co-sell credits / partner incentives: If Redwood pursues co-sell credits with AWS/Azure/GCP on your behalf, that can reduce our gross price and therefore your net cost, but these credits are not guaranteed and timing can be multiple months. Co-sell incentives often require joint account planning and sales motion documentation.
- Migration plan: We map marketplace entitlements to Redwood account entitlements, apply a credit for prepaid marketplace spend, and transition billing to Redwood invoices on the agreed date. We typically include a 30-day overlap window to ensure usage reconciliation.

Recommendation (ops): Do a private offer on the cloud marketplace to enable PO-based buying and faster procurement onboarding, and include a short pilot credit line to cover marketplace fees. Then sign a direct vendor contract before the renewal of the pilot to lock in committed discounts and SLAs if required.

Hi Liam — thanks for surfacing this. Short customer-facing summary and proposed next steps below.

Executive summary (1 paragraph): For a fast pilot we recommend Redwood issue a cloud private offer (AWS Private Offer preferred if Nimbus is primarily on AWS). That path preserves PO-based consolidated billing on your side, allows us to negotiate a private price (reducing the marketplace list premium), and enables a relatively quick start (typically 7–21 days for vendor onboarding + creating the private offer). At renewal we convert to a direct vendor agreement to capture committed discounts and attach SLA addenda if required.

Operational checklist & timeline:
- Procurement pre-reqs (2–3 business days): share Nimbus vendor onboarding form and PO template with us.
- Legal/DPA (3–7 business days typical): we will provide standard DPA + SOC 2 report; bespoke residency or audit clauses may add time.
- Private offer creation (3–5 business days): Redwood creates a private offer in AWS with negotiated pricing and adds Nimbus as the eligible buyer.
- Start pilot (after PO & private offer): typical pilot start window 7–21 days from kick-off.

Key commercial notes:
- Estimated marketplace fee impact: ~12% of list price (will confirm exact percent by cloud provider). Redwood proposes to apply a one-time pilot credit equal to 50% of estimated marketplace fees for the first 3 months of pilot usage.
- Co-sell: we will pursue co-sell credits with our cloud partner in parallel; any realized credits reduce net pricing moving forward.
- Migration: We will provide a credit for marketplace spend when moving to a direct contract so there is no double-charging.

Requested next steps from Nimbus:
1) Confirm you want an AWS private offer (or indicate alternative cloud).
2) Send your vendor onboarding form and PO template to procurement@nimbusanalytics.com and cc irene.
3) Confirm availability for a 30-minute kickoff call Thursday 18th or Friday 19th (we can flex).

If you confirm, we will prepare a short SOW and private-offer pricing sheet and send a DocuSign for signature where needed.

Best regards,
